text.p: Foods group Inno-Pacific Holdings Ltd said on Monday it was proposing a renounceable right issue of new shares on the basis of three rights shares for every one ordinary share held.
The issue would raise net proceeds of about Singapore $211.44 million, the company said in a statement.
The rights issue was subject to approval by the Stock Exchange of Singapore and the company's shareholders, it said.
Proceeds from the issue would used to finance acquisition of commercial and industrial buildings and for working capital.
The rights issue would result in the creation of 710.46 million new shares.
The company would also issue 59.20 million free detachable warrants on the basis of one warrant for four shares held.

The company said its managing director, Malaysian entrepreneur Soh Chee Wen, through a private company, had agreed to underwrite 75 percent of the issue. Two banks would underwrite the remaining 25 percent of the issue.
If the issue resulted in Soh, who now owns 18.32 percent of the company's stock, owning more than 25 percent, he would make a general takeover offer for the company, the statement said.
